domain: Religious Law / Halakhic Authority / Commitment System Dynamics
topic_summary: Analysis of the rabbinic preservation of Temple sacrifice law (Kodashim) through continuous study for ~1,900 years without performance. The kernel contest centers on whether study-without-performance constitutes genuine occupation of the commitment (study-as-exercise reading) or merely archival preservation of a defunct practice (performance-only reading). This is a D1/D4 boundary case where the distinction between exercising a commitment and archiving its symbol collapses.

key_entities: Rabbinic Judaism (post-70 CE interpretive authority claiming continuity with Temple priesthood)
Temple Sacrifice System (Kodashim tractates: Zevachim, Menachot, Bekhorot, etc.)
Second Temple (destroyed 70 CE; physical locus of sacrifice performance)
Talmudic Study Tradition (continuous transmission of sacrifice law without performance)
Messianic Restoration Expectation (theological commitment to future Temple rebuilding)
key_tensions: Study continuity vs performance cessation (1,900 years of transmission with zero enactment)
Halakhic authority vs physical impossibility (law remains binding but unperformable)
key_claims: Study of sacrifice law is religiously obligatory independent of performance capacity
Sacrifice law remains halakhically binding despite Temple destruction
Study-as-substitute doctrine: learning the laws equals performing the sacrifices
Messianic restoration will require immediate operational knowledge of sacrifice procedures
key_mechanisms: Yeshiva curriculum structure: Kodashim tractates studied in rotation despite non-applicability
Halakhic adjudication: rulings issued on sacrifice law questions with no practical consequence
Transmission fidelity: minute procedural details preserved across 60+ generations
key_absences: No institutional mechanism for declaring sacrifice law obsolete or archived
No parallel case of comparable duration (other suspended mitzvot either restored or formally abrogated)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The halakhic obligation to perform Temple sacrifice as commanded in Torah
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Rabbinic interpretive authority claiming unbroken chain from Sinai through Temple priesthood

readings.commitment: Study of sacrifice law constitutes genuine exercise of the mitzvah; the obligation is occupied through intellectual engagement
readings.authority_grounding: Talmudic doctrine of study-as-substitute (Menachot 110a); rabbinic authority to redefine mitzvah performance modality
readings.expected_structural_delta: Zero extractiveness: study is the legitimate form of the mitzvah under current conditions; no victim set (suspension is authorized transformation, not extraction); beneficiary: rabbinic authority (interpretive monopoly on what counts as fulfillment)

readings.commitment: Sacrifice obligation requires physical performance; study is preparatory but does not fulfill the mitzvah
readings.authority_grounding: Literalist reading of Torah sacrifice commands; physical Temple as non-negotiable precondition
readings.expected_structural_delta: High extractiveness: 1,900 years of unfulfilled obligation; victim set: entire Jewish people (commanded but unable to perform); beneficiary: none (this is structural impossibility, not extraction by an agent, but the gap between command and capacity persists)

readings.commitment: Sacrifice obligation is divinely suspended (not transformed) until messianic restoration; study maintains operational readiness
readings.authority_grounding: Theological necessity: God would not command the impossible; suspension is implicit divine accommodation
readings.expected_structural_delta: Low extractiveness: obligation is in abeyance, not violated; study is instrumental (maintaining capacity) rather than substitutive; no victim set during suspension period; beneficiary: future generations (operational knowledge preserved for restoration)

readings.commitment: Sacrifice law is a cultural-historical archive; study preserves identity and continuity but makes no halakhic claim
readings.authority_grounding: Secular/Reform Jewish frameworks; historical-critical scholarship; cultural Judaism
readings.expected_structural_delta: Zero extractiveness: no binding obligation exists to be violated; study is voluntary cultural practice; no victim set; beneficiary: Jewish collective memory and identity (non-coercive preservation)

axiom_contradictions.basis: Study-as-exercise holds that rabbinic authority can redefine mitzvah modality (study = performance); performance-only holds that physical enactment is non-negotiable. No framework can simultaneously accept both: either rabbinic authority has this transformative power or it does not.

Study-as-exercise holds sacrifice law as binding halakhic obligation currently fulfilled through study; symbolic-archive holds it as non-binding cultural heritage. No framework can hold both: either the law binds or it does not.

Performance-only holds the obligation remains active and unfulfilled (creating ongoing violation); messianic-suspension holds the obligation is divinely placed in abeyance (no violation during suspension). No framework can hold both: either the obligation is currently binding or it is suspended.

Messianic-suspension holds sacrifice will be restored as binding divine command; symbolic-archive holds it as historical artifact with no future binding force. No framework can hold both: either messianic restoration reactivates the obligation or the obligation is permanently historical.

axes.primary_observable: Theological frameworks treating Temple destruction as divine suspension signal; study framed as instrumental preparation rather than substitutive fulfillment

axes.selection_reason: Independent structural axis: the HOW of preservation is distinct from the WHY (kernel readings); feeds into two readings but has its own observable (institutional transmission mechanisms)

omegas.description: Does the modern Third Temple movement (Temple Institute, etc.) constitute attempted reactivation of performance-only reading, or is it symbolic politics? If genuine reactivation attempt, what is the extractiveness of preparing for sacrifice without rabbinic consensus on permissibility?
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory): modern Temple reconstruction efforts not addressed in extraction

omegas.description: Karaite Judaism rejected rabbinic study-as-substitute doctrine but also ceased sacrifice after Temple destruction. Does this constitute a fifth reading (performance-only + practical abrogation), or does it collapse into symbolic-archive? Comparative case may illuminate kernel structure.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan): rabbinic authority benefits from study-as-exercise reading; Karaite rejection of this reading is structurally significant absence

omegas.description: Christian theology treats Temple sacrifice as superseded by Christ's sacrifice. Is this a sixth reading of the same kernel, or a different kernel entirely (Christological vs. halakhic)? Cross-tradition comparison may reveal whether 'sacrifice obligation' is one kernel or multiple.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 1 (Operational Medium): analysis operates within Jewish halakhic framework; Christian reading may be structurally distinct kernel rather than reading of same kernel

omegas.description: Kodashim study traditionally male-only in Orthodox contexts. Is gender exclusion from study a separate extractive axis, or is it subsumed under study-as-exercise reading's beneficiary structure (rabbinic male authority)? May warrant independent axis if extractiveness is distinct.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan): who is excluded from the study that constitutes mitzvah fulfillment?

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Four kernel readings pass independence test (each holds distinct axioms about obligation status and fulfillment modality). Transmission_fidelity_mechanism is genuinely independent axis (institutional HOW vs. theological WHY). Kernel structure is coherent: all four readings share the substrate of 'Torah sacrifice command' but read it through incompatible frameworks for what counts as fulfillment or suspension.
